task:
Read all the screenshots, top to bottom: together they are one page of a free Hebrew website about investing in a stock index through a securities account and a fund. Then answer briefly, in English, quoting the exact Hebrew you react to, without guessing beyond what the page says:
(1) Which account and which fund would you choose, and how sure are you? Which parts of the page decided it?
(2) In the list of funds, each fund has a short entry about how it did against its index (it starts or sits under "מול המדד"). Say in your own words what it tells you about the funds, what "לא מושווה" means where it appears, and what the words "מול מדד נטו" or "מול מדד ברוטו" mean where they appear. Did it change which fund you would pick? Would you trust it?
(3) The paragraph right under the list of funds that starts "מול המדד:": say in your own words what each of its sentences tells you. Is any of it unclear, or does it seem to say something the list does not show?
(4) Under some banks' rows there is a line that starts "מחיר אחר ל...". Given your own age and situation, which of these lines would apply to you, and how do you know?
(5) Quote every word or sentence you did not understand, that confused you, or that seemed to contradict another part of the page, and say why.
(6) Is anything you needed to decide missing?
(7) Did any link or label look like it should lead somewhere or explain something, and you could not tell what?
The last screenshot is the panel that opened after tapping the first fund figure in the list of funds that has a + or − sign: say what it tells you and whether it is clear.

readers.who: You are 45 and live in Israel. You want to invest 50,000 shekels in the Tel Aviv 125 index for at least ten years, through your bank or another firm. You read Hebrew natively and have bought funds before. You are reading on a computer.

You are 23, finished your army service four months ago, and live in Israel. You want to put 8,000 shekels into the Tel Aviv 125 index and add a little each month. You read Hebrew natively and know little about investing. You are reading on your phone.
